lead: Wing boxes and fuselage frames are stiffened by stringers. For bending stress, the skin between stringers mainly carries shear, so direct stress is taken by stringer areas called booms. This chapter reduces the section to booms at known x and y, finds the boom centroid and second moments from boom areas alone, then applies the unsymmetrical bending formula boom by boom. A skew load needs both M_x and M_y; an unsymmetric section adds I_xy. Only a few universities teach this, but it is how a real wing box is checked.
prereq: You need Chapter 4.2, Chapter 4.4, and Unit 1 for the bending moment distribution along a wing or fuselage.

blocks.text: Replace each stringer and its attached skin by a boom of area A_i at coordinates x_i, y_i. Leave out the skin between booms for direct stress; it carries mainly shear, as Chapter 4.4 explains. Find the boom centroid: x̄ = ΣA_i x_i / ΣA_i and ȳ = ΣA_i y_i / ΣA_i. Move the origin there. Then compute I_xx = ΣA_i y_i², I_yy = ΣA_i x_i² and I_xy = ΣA_i x_i y_i. Use m² for A and m for x and y; I is then in m⁴. These are second moments of the boom areas only. If the booms are symmetric about both centroidal axes, I_xy = 0. So is the case with symmetry about one axis only, since the boom pairs then cancel ΣA x y. I_xy is non-zero only when the layout has no such symmetry; then the centroidal axes are not principal and must be rotated by the standard principal-axis formula. The figure's four booms are symmetric, so I_xy cancels.

Take M_x positive when it produces tension at positive y, and M_y positive when it produces tension at positive x. Then σ = M_x y/I_xx + M_y x/I_yy. Here M_x and M_y are in N·m, x and y in m, I in m⁴, and σ in Pa. The neutral axis is σ=0: M_x y / I_xx + M_y x / I_yy = 0, a straight line through the centroid tilted by the skew moment. For an unsymmetric boom layout use σ = [(M_x I_yy − M_y I_xy)y + (M_y I_xx − M_x I_xy)x] / (I_xx I_yy − I_xy²). The equations are identical; only I_xy is non-zero. For a stringer-stiffened wing, M_x(z) and M_y(z) come from Unit 1's shear force and bending moment distribution. Quote the moment at the section; do not re-derive it. Apply the formula at every boom. The same steps serve a fuselage frame or a tail plane.

figure.caption: Four equal booms under M_x=10 kN·m and M_y=4 kN·m. The diagonal pair reaches +158 MPa and −158 MPa; the other pair is only ±92 MPa.

spec.title: Booms: x, y, A, sigma
spec.aria: Four booms of equal area, listed with their x and y coordinates in millimetres and the direct stress each carries under a skew moment, showing that the diagonal pair is most heavily loaded.

examples.question: A wing box is idealised into four booms of area 200 mm² at (150, 100), (−150, 100), (−150, −100) and (150, −100) mm. All coordinates are in millimetres. It carries M_x = 10 kN·m and M_y = 4 kN·m. Find the stress in each boom.
steps: Boom centroid: x̄=ΣA x/ΣA=0 and ȳ=ΣA y/ΣA=0, so the origin is the centroid.
examples.answer: The boom stresses are 158 MPa, 92 MPa, −158 MPa and −92 MPa at booms 1 to 4, to the nearest MPa.
examples.check:
A=200e-6
x=[0.15,-0.15,-0.15,0.15]
y=[0.1,0.1,-0.1,-0.1]
Mx=10e3
My=4e3
Ixx=sum(A*yy**2 for yy in y)
Iyy=sum(A*xx**2 for xx in x)
for xx,yy in zip(x,y):
    s=(Mx*yy/Ixx + My*xx/Iyy)/1e6
    print(int(round(s)))

traps: Using the centroid of the skin outline instead of the centroid of the boom areas puts the reference axes in the wrong place; this changes I_xx, I_yy and I_xy and therefore changes every boom stress.
Leaving I_xy out for an unsymmetric boom layout and using σ=M_x y/I_xx + M_y x/I_yy; this is valid only when I_xy=0.
Mixing millimetres with N·m; convert A to m² and x,y to m before computing I and σ.
Applying full skin area as direct stress instead of reducing it to boom areas; this overestimates I and underestimates stress.

quiz.q: Why is skin between stringers left out of direct bending stress?
quiz.a: It carries mainly shear; boom areas carry direct stress.

quiz.q: What does I_xy=0 mean for a boom section?
quiz.a: The centroidal axes are principal; M_x alone gives σ=M_x y/I_xx and M_y alone gives σ=M_y x/I_yy.

quiz.q: Four booms A=100 mm² at (±100, ±50) mm. Find I_xx and I_yy.
Why does a skew moment load one diagonal pair more?
quiz.a: The two terms add when x and y have the same sign and subtract when signs differ.

quiz.q: Which terms couple M_x and M_y when I_xy≠0?
quiz.a: With I_xy≠0 each moment acts on both coordinates: M_x produces stress varying with x through the −M_x I_xy x term and M_y produces stress varying with y through the −M_y I_xy y term. That is what couples M_x and M_y.

quiz.q: Which Unit 1 input is needed at a wing section?
quiz.a: Bending moment components M_x(z) and M_y(z) at that spanwise station from the shear force and bending moment distribution.

beyond: Not for the exam. In industry, wing-box direct stress is checked with boom idealisations before detailed finite element models. Search for “boom idealisation wing box”, “unsymmetrical bending stringers”, and “direct stress wing skin”. Newer curricula link this to shear flow and shear centre in Unit 5.
